git add internal/testenv/ethos.go && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(testenv): materialize implement.yaml instead of symlinking archetypes

CI's first run of this tier caught a genuine dev/CI divergence in the
harness itself (run 33353470073): IsolateEthos symlinked the global
archetypes tree from $HOME/.punt-labs/ethos/archetypes into the scratch
home. A developer's machine typically has that tree; a clean CI runner
does not, and this repo carries no .punt-labs/ethos/archetypes/ either.
The symlink dangled, ethos loaded zero archetypes, and every generated
contract was rejected as an unknown mission type -- ambient developer
state, exactly what this design names as the hard constraint to
eliminate. kth flagged this exact class in round 1 of the design review
and it went unclosed.

Fix: materialize a hand-written implement.yaml into the scratch tree,
identically in dev and CI, rather than falling back to synthesis only
when the global tree is absent. A conditional fallback would make dev
and CI run against different archetype data -- the same divergence
class this tier exists to catch -- and would mean this specific failure
could never be reproduced locally again.

"implement" is the only archetype needed: neither BuildContract nor
buildStageContract (mission.go, pipeline.go) ever sets an explicit
mission type, so every contract this tier generates defaults to it.

Verified by reproducing CI's condition locally rather than trusting
`make check` on a machine that already has the global tree: ran the
affected tests with $HOME pointed at an empty directory (no
.punt-labs/ethos at all).
  Before this fix: TestBuildStageContract_ValidatesAgainstRealEthosCLI
    and TestOnNewMail_EndToEnd both fail with the identical CI error
    ("unknown mission type \"implement\"; available archetypes: ").
  After this fix: both pass under the same clean-$HOME condition.
EOF
)"

tool_input.message:
Three Copilot findings on PR #261. I verified each against the current head (`d70be17`) — two valid, one partly stale but with a real residue. Same branch, commit, don't push.

**1. `Makefile:88` — `make test` is not self-contained. Valid, and the most important of the three.**

```make
tools-ethos:
	go install github.com/punt-labs/ethos/v4/cmd/ethos@$(ETHOS_VERSION)

test: tools-ethos
	go test -race -count=1 ./...
```

`go install` puts the binary in `$(go env GOPATH)/bin`, and the recipe never ensures that is on `PATH`. The tests find it with `exec.LookPath("ethos")`. So on a machine whose `PATH` lacks `GOPATH/bin`: provisioning succeeds, tests fail with "ethos not found on PATH", and our own remedy message tells the developer to run `make tools-ethos` — which they just ran. A closed loop with no way out except reading our source.

This is the same class as the archetype bug you just fixed: it works on my machine and in CI (where the workflow amends `$GITHUB_PATH`) and fails for someone whose environment differs. Prepend `$(go env GOPATH)/bin` to `PATH` in the `test` recipe so `make test` is genuinely self-contained and matches what CI does. Consider whether `GOBIN` should take precedence when set, since `go install` honors it.

**2. `internal/testenv/ethos.go:121` — the stated claim is stale, the underlying point is not.**

Copilot says `IsolateEthos` symlinks `~/.punt-labs/ethos/archetypes` without an existence check. That symlink is gone — you removed it in `d70be17` and I confirmed `os.UserHomeDir()` is no longer called at all.

But line 128 still does `os.Symlink` for the *repo* subtrees (`identities`, `personalities`, `roles`, `teams`, `talents`, `writing-styles`) with no existence check. Severity is much lower than the global-tree case, because those are committed repo content present in any checkout including CI — not ambient developer state. Still worth closing: `os.Symlink` succeeds against a nonexistent target, so a missing or renamed subtree becomes a confusing failure deep inside ethos rather than a clear one at the point of setup.

Add the check and fail with a message naming the missing path. Reply to that thread noting the global-archetypes half is already fixed — I want the record to show which part was stale rather than accepting a finding that no longer applies.

**3. `docs/daemon-test-harness.md:5` — valid, trivial.**

Header still reads "Status: proposed… Produces no code — this document is the contract for a follow-on implementation mission." That mission is `m-2026-08-31-002`, closed pass, and this PR is the implementation. Update the status to reflect that it is implemented, and cite the implementing mission and PR so a reader lands on the right place.

**Do not weaken anything to make these pass.** In particular, don't resolve #1 by changing the tests to use an absolute path to the binary — the whole point of `exec.LookPath` is that it exercises the same resolution production uses.

`make check`, commit, do not push. Report each fix, and for #2 tell me explicitly what you found the repo subtree situation to be.
